title: I got 10 animated 2D characters out of one AI video generation ($0.05 each)
author: Bill_Buffet
selftext:
I'm building a Godot game that needs hundreds of NPCs in a hand-drawn cartoon style, and I've been testing ways to animate AI-generated characters cheaply.

**What worked:**

1. Design each character with an image model, using the first character as the style reference (\~$0.04 each).
2. Put 10 of them on one green-screen frame in fixed slots (2 rows × 5).
3. One image-to-video generation (Seedance 2.0 Fast via OpenRouter, 720p, 5 s, $0.46) with the prompt "everyone walks in place, don't interact".
4. A Python/ffmpeg script crops each slot, keys out the green, aligns the feet, finds the most seamless loop, and exports Godot SpriteFrames.

**Cost per character walk:** 1 per clip = $0.46, 3 per clip = $0.15, 10 per clip = $0.046. Quality holds at game size (\~200 px tall). Up close, the 10-per-clip version is a bit softer.

Before this, I tried a cut-out bone rig (free and unlimited, but it looked like a paper puppet) and one video per character (looks great, but too expensive at scale).

**What's your approach for animating hundreds of 2D characters?**

comments.author: Lumpy_Conference6640
comments.body: Really good, except if you have too many objects working at the same time, you do see more hallucinatory behavior. I think the addendum is that general NPCs do a sprite sheet array animation, but individual ones let main characters, maybe focus. What do you think? Good tutorials!

replies.author: Bill_Buffet
replies.body: Agreed, the main protagonists deserves dedicated video generation. But for minor characters who only appear on screen for a few seconds, it seems like a smart way to cut costs.

comments.author: Droooomp
comments.body:
Its good if you need simple animations, not good if you need complex animations, the more you fit in the canvas the higher the chance to have hallucinations.  
Make all of them do pirouettes  or stuff that needs the model to generate the backside or stuff that does not exist, youll see it crack and start to hallucinate more or less depending on the model.

replies.author: Bill_Buffet
replies.body:
Interesting idea! I tried it a few times, and yes: the more complex the movement, the fewer characters you can fit in one scene without hallucinations.

https://reddit.com/link/1xsvbmr/video/zjokn6qoju0i1/player

replies.author: Droooomp
replies.body:
Yes, , i use the smallest h3 minimax locally, its something i discovered due to having the luxury to spam it. But for now this is how i see it there is an interchangeable limit of context you can feed it, considering that all the layers inside the network share the same "language" i could only say that you have to balance movement overtime(generating stuff that you cant see in the start or end frame), complexity of movement (basically directing tge model with timestamps) and complexity of image(one two three etc things that need move or bg animation also), and immutable stuff like audio and also whatever each model has extra in the layers, all these in a "pot" if the pot spills over it hallucinates.

But If you focus on only one or two of those things it does it well(ofdc bigger models can do more), even google omni the cheapest model(and capable to drive animation from image) does it really well, but once you spread it and start to mix them and "ask" multiple things at once (complex animation, bg animation, directed movement and so on) it starts to hallucinate. 

Your particular case has 2 things that help the model, a similar animation for all and only a matteable collor on the bg, you could play and test it to see where does the model crack.

replies.author: Bill_Buffet

comments.author: CashFirm573
comments.body: Just map the base model image to json with parts and mocap it for free in 1 prompt, no 3rd party tools needed, then have AI procedurally generate it and if you want sprite sheet export it into png, this way it keeps consistency between all designs. If anything cause AI has really good vision, make you're attack animations using Seeddance 2.0 and then take those videos feed it to Claude, with proper vision tech and ask it to use that for X animation.
